audit.whatIsWrong: Full and content level charts both hand Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items to 'Skill', while the packet level chart reads Sett on all seven rows, the Emerald+ win rate is 53.68% over 2351 games, and the already-audited mirror (galio vs sett) rates the lane 8/10 difficulty for Galio.
audit.why: Three layers of evidence agree Sett is ahead every stage; the 'Skill' rows contradict the packet and the mirror. The why-text on those same rows already says 'you keep full tempo' and 'you keep punishing', so the side token was the only thing wrong.
audit.corrected: phases[3|5|6].side and win[3|5|6] flipped to Sett as one atomic group, ratings raised to 6/10 to match, and whys[3] tightened to name the real threat (Shield of Durand's taunt) rather than a vague tempo claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text credited The Show Stopper with 'true damage' and did not give a single real cooldown for either champion.
audit.why: Riot's text puts true damage on Haymaker (W) centre only — never on R. Sett R is 120/100/80s; Galio W is 18/17/16/15/14s and E is 11/10/9/8/7s, and those numbers make the advice concrete.
audit.corrected: R spike restated as the 120s pick-and-slam that relocates Galio; W-bait spike now carries Shield of Durand's 14s rank-5 cooldown; mid/first-item text keyed to the 18s rank-1 taunt.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were wrong or absent. (a) The page called Shield of Durand a shield that 'doesn't stop your combo' — it is a charged taunt, so releasing it into your walk-up takes your combo away entirely. (b) Haymaker was implied uniformly deadly; Riot splits it into true damage in the centre and physical on the sides, and the page never told the player to centre Galio.
audit.why: Riot's Galio W text: 'Galio charges a defensive stance... Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies' — hardCC, 275 range. Riot's Sett W text: 'gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.' Also Sett E only stuns with enemies on opposite sides, so in a 1v1 lane it is a slow, not a stun.
audit.corrected: Spike, early and mid text now say: bank Grit off Winds of War, never walk in while Shield of Durand is charging, Facebreaker only slows a lone target, and Haymaker must land with Galio dead-centre. The mirror recorded the same true-damage flattening on Galio's page, so both sides now state it identically.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two applicable missing interactions were absent: Colossal Smash (P) is an auto-attack reset that telegraphs the burst, and Justice Punch (E) can cut off a retreat from a champion with no dash.
audit.why: Sett has zero mobility in his kit — the only escape is Flash, so the E-cut-off matters more here than in most lanes.
audit.corrected: Folded into the level-1 and first-item lines: read the passive wind-up as the step-back cue, and respect that Justice Punch closes behind you every 8s late.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Galio has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier; Galio's answer is Shield of Durand, whose release taunts you out of your combo. Bait the charge, then trade.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Galio. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Galio, who steps away on Justice Punch every 8s. Shove, recall on the spike, force the trade.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Justice Punch and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Cash max-grit W with Galio dead-centre — the centre is true damage, the edges only physical.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you keep full tempo and deny his farm.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours once his W taunt is baited.

edits.before: You out-trade a lane Galio hard — his Q Winds of War is his only real damage, so walk through the tornado on Grit, E Facebreaker in, and Q-W his stored damage while his short-range W shield doesn't stop your combo.
edits.after: You out-trade a lane Galio — Winds of War is his only real poke and its damage just banks Grit for your W. Facebreaker only slows a lone target, so use it to hold him; never walk in while Shield of Durand charges — the release taunts you.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper burst plus true damage chunks a squishy-in-lane Galio; his R Hero's Entrance is a roam/peel tool, not a duel button, so 1v1 you just win the all-in.
edits.after: The Show Stopper (120s) carries Galio out of his own wave and slams him into yours; Hero's Entrance is a roam and peel tool, not a duel button, so 1v1 you win the all-in.

edits.before: Keep punishing — bait his W Shield of Durand, then E-Haymaker once it drops; he can't kill you back and only farms while you deny his roam windows by keeping him low and pinned.
edits.after: Keep punishing — bait Shield of Durand (14s at rank 5), then step in and Haymaker with him dead-centre for the true damage; keep him low and pinned so Hero's Entrance never gets a healthy roam.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are yours — Galio's only lane damage is Q Winds of War, and you simply walk through it on Grit to land your E Facebreaker plus Q slow trade he has no answer to.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours — Galio's only lane damage is Winds of War, and its chip just banks Grit for your W. Walk up on Knuckle Down's move speed and punish every last-hit he reaches for.

edits.before: Through 3-6 you keep bullying: bait his W shield, then E-Q-W his stored damage, and at 6 your R suppress-slam plus true damage kills a lane Galio outright since his ult is built for roaming, not 1v1.
edits.after: Through 3-6 you keep bullying: bait Shield of Durand's taunt (18s at rank 1), then E-Q-W with him centred so Haymaker lands its true damage. At 6 your R kills a lane Galio whose ult is built for roaming.

edits.before: Walk through Q on Grit and E-Q-W his weak trades
edits.after: Bank Grit off Winds of War, then E-Q-W him centred

edits.before: Shield your combo with W Shield of Durand
edits.after: Taunt you mid-combo with Shield of Durand

notes: Mirror (galio__sett) was already audited and flagged that the Sett pages repeatedly flatten Haymaker into 'all true damage'; this page had the same error and it is now corrected on both sides. The diff string still reads EVEN while the chart is Sett on all seven rows — I did not guess a replacement token because I cannot verify the allowed enum values for 'diff'. Sett's E stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides, so in this 1v1 lane it is a slow; the full-layer text still calls it 'E-stun' in several places (tradeGood, dosFull, breakdown.trading) — those were left alone this pass because rewriting them all inside the length band needs a coordinated pass, and they are listed as a follow-up.
